title: In my 6G private campus network, ensure ultra-reliable low-latency communication for 500 industrial robots with end-to-end latency below 1 ms and reliability of 99.9999% while keeping energy consumption under 500 kWh per day.

metadata.notes: Classic URLLC 6G use-case; matches TR290 DeliveryExpectation

nl_intent: In my 6G private campus network, ensure ultra-reliable low-latency communication for 500 industrial robots with end-to-end latency below 1 ms and reliability of 99.9999% while keeping energy consumption under 500 kWh per day.

tmf921_intent.name: URLLC-Robots-Campus
tmf921_intent.description: Ultra-reliable low-latency intent for industrial robots in 6G campus

title: For the AI-orchestrated 6G core in my campus, minimize total energy consumption of all network functions while maintaining at least 10 Gbps aggregate throughput and 99.99% availability.

metadata.notes: Energy vs performance trade-off; uses utility function per TR290

nl_intent: For the AI-orchestrated 6G core in my campus, minimize total energy consumption of all network functions while maintaining at least 10 Gbps aggregate throughput and 99.99% availability.

title: Deploy a new eMBB slice for 2000 AR/VR users in the 6G campus with guaranteed 500 Mbps per user and 99.999% reliability, but only if it does not exceed 30% of total RAN resources.
nl_intent: Deploy a new eMBB slice for 2000 AR/VR users in the 6G campus with guaranteed 500 Mbps per user and 99.999% reliability, but only if it does not exceed 30% of total RAN resources.

title: In case of detected congestion in the 6G campus RAN, automatically reconfigure mMTC slices for 10000 IoT sensors to reduce their duty cycle to 10% while preserving 99.9% packet delivery ratio.
nl_intent: In case of detected congestion in the 6G campus RAN, automatically reconfigure mMTC slices for 10000 IoT sensors to reduce their duty cycle to 10% while preserving 99.9% packet delivery ratio.

title: Ensure predictive assurance for all critical 6G URLLC slices: any predicted latency violation >0.5 ms must trigger proactive resource reallocation within 100 ms.
nl_intent: Ensure predictive assurance for all critical 6G URLLC slices: any predicted latency violation >0.5 ms must trigger proactive resource reallocation within 100 ms.

title: Create two conflicting intents: one for maximum throughput in eMBB and one for minimum energy; resolve via negotiation with priority to energy if carbon budget is exceeded.

metadata.notes: Explicit conflict example for testing negotiation

nl_intent: Create two conflicting intents: one for maximum throughput in eMBB and one for minimum energy; resolve via negotiation with priority to energy if carbon budget is exceeded.

title: In the 6G multi-domain campus (RAN + transport + core), guarantee end-to-end latency <2 ms for 100 autonomous vehicles with 99.9999% reliability across all domains.
nl_intent: In the 6G multi-domain campus (RAN + transport + core), guarantee end-to-end latency <2 ms for 100 autonomous vehicles with 99.9999% reliability across all domains.

title: For my 6G testbed, report on intent fulfillment every 5 minutes and notify if any KPI deviates more than 5% from target.
nl_intent: For my 6G testbed, report on intent fulfillment every 5 minutes and notify if any KPI deviates more than 5% from target.

title: Suspend all non-critical slices in the 6G campus during a power outage alert while preserving URLLC slices at full capacity.
nl_intent: Suspend all non-critical slices in the 6G campus during a power outage alert while preserving URLLC slices at full capacity.

title: Optimize 6G RAN beamforming for 99.99% coverage in the campus while limiting total transmit power to 40 dBm per site.
nl_intent: Optimize 6G RAN beamforming for 99.99% coverage in the campus while limiting total transmit power to 40 dBm per site.

title: Ensure zero-touch failover for all 6G intents: if any intent report shows degradation, automatically migrate to backup resources within 50 ms.
nl_intent: Ensure zero-touch failover for all 6G intents: if any intent report shows degradation, automatically migrate to backup resources within 50 ms.

title: In the 6G campus, allow dynamic negotiation between two intents: one for maximum user density and one for minimum interference; accept the compromise that maximizes overall utility.
nl_intent: In the 6G campus, allow dynamic negotiation between two intents: one for maximum user density and one for minimum interference; accept the compromise that maximizes overall utility.

title: Provide a partial intent for testing: guarantee only reliability >99.999% for URLLC robots; all other KPIs are best-effort.
nl_intent: Provide a partial intent for testing: guarantee only reliability >99.999% for URLLC robots; all other KPIs are best-effort.

title: For AI-native 6G orchestration, translate this natural language request into a valid TMF921 intent that can be directly posted to the /intent endpoint.
nl_intent: For AI-native 6G orchestration, translate this natural language request into a valid TMF921 intent that can be directly posted to the /intent endpoint.

title: Monitor and report fulfillment of all active intents in the 6G campus every 60 seconds via the hub subscription mechanism.
nl_intent: Monitor and report fulfillment of all active intents in the 6G campus every 60 seconds via the hub subscription mechanism.

Condition objects are introduced and replace parameters. Conditions are more generic and re-useable in other cases where logical evaluations are needed, for example in context.

title: TR290_Intent_Common_Model_v3.0.0
text: is chapter provides a brief overview of the most significant conceptual changes between model versions to illustrate the evolution of intent modeling. An iteration of the major model number indicates revisions with substantial conceptual changes. An iteration of intermediate model number indicates minor additions, while the overall concept of the model are kept. The minor model number iterates if error corrections are needed. 1.2.1. Model version 3 The third major version of the intent common model introduces functions for expressing operators. Functions provide a more intuitive way to express requirements. They also improve precision in the logical expression. Condition objects are introduced and replace parameters. Conditions are more generic and re-useable in other cases where logical evaluations are needed, for example in context. 1.2.2. Model version 2 The second major version of the intent common model introduces the concept of providing requirements through logical conditions. If and when a condition is evaluated as true, the system is compliant to the requirement.
